title: Introducing Tessl: The Package Manager for Coding Agent Skills
description:
As AI leaders, developers need a package manager for skills and context. Tessl promises just that, optimizing how AI agents integrate with your software development workflow. Skills, the building blocks of agent behavior, risk becoming obsolete as libraries evolve and models change. Maintaining these skills goes beyond mere documentation — it's about ensuring effectiveness and relevance over time. Tessl provides this infrastructure, allowing you to version, test, and continuously improve your agent skills. It sounds ambitious. It delivers results.

Tessl is a platform for developing, evaluating, and distributing agent skills and context as software — versioned, testable, and continuously improved.

But now, Tessl helps you build a software factory as well.

Tessl's plugin registry makes sure your agentic workflows scale across the company: catching insecure or low-quality skills before they ship, enforcing standards across every agent and repo, and turning one engineer's automation into a reusable asset for the whole org, without locking into a single vendor.

What we cover:
• Optimize agent skills for up to 3.3× improved API usage across open-source libraries
• Tessl's capability to install, manage, and update agent skills without duplication
• The role of tessl.json in tracking installed skills and their updates
• How does Tessl help evaluate and optimize your own skill development?
• Ensuring your organization's agents receive the right context at the right time

🌐 Try Tessl - we help you build a software factory, one step at a time: https://tessl.io
🔔 Subscribe for weekly episodes on AI-native development
